point3_verdict.real_in_shipped_game: Real but transient; the long-lived staleness is a harness artifact.
evidence: ship_geometry_demo.gd:329-334 and 635: in the live game journey_map.auto_tick=false and the demo calls journey_tick() -> map.tick() at 20 Hz with sim.pipelined=true. tick() drains, sends a pipelined heartbeat, then refresh()es on the pre-reply world, so _last_view equals sim.world as of that moment. The in-flight reply lands only at the next drain.

Any other caller that sends/drains advances sim.world with no map refresh: ship_consoles.gd:316 journey_sim.send([intent],0.0) on a committed course, the replan sends inside tick() itself, solar_departure.gd:160. In the shipped game the next map tick (<= 50 ms) refreshes, so the label is stale for at most one tick.

In the scripted harness journey_auto_tick=false and every child _process is disabled, so nothing refreshes until the script ticks again; after arrival that is multiple samples (1206 vs 1208). That is why the audit saw 10 samples. The audit was right that _last_view can lag sim.world; it overstated how long this lasts in the real game.
The self-heal in galaxy_map._process runs in the real game because the map node's own _process is enabled (auto_tick false only skips the accum loop, which sits after the self-heal).
correctness_and_safety: Fires only when int(_last_view.tick) != int(sim.world.tick); refresh() writes _last_view from sim.world so it converges in one call. While a pipelined tick is in flight sim.world does not change, so no refresh loop and at most one extra refresh per tick.
A sim whose world lacks 'tick': both sides default to -1; before the first refresh _last_view is {} so -1==-1 and nothing fires; with sim==null the guard short-circuits. No crash.

refresh() does not touch hold_s/_holding/_queue/_pending, so hold_commit is unaffected; the self-heal runs after hold_commit in the same frame and a commit queued by it is still sent by the next tick().
guided_read_only: refresh() only sets button disabled states from it; safe, and in the guided tour the map is read-only anyway.

Cost: refresh() rebuilds ~20 labels plus _refresh_system_list; at most doubles refresh cost on frames in which a non-map caller moved the world (<= 20/s). I did not benchmark it; the perf pass #240 pipelining is not undone because the self-heal never drains or sends.

point4_verdict: Harness call journey_map._process(0.0) after demo._process in step() faithfully emulates the engine's per-frame hook the harness disabled. With delta 0: _holding hold_commit adds 0 s (no commit); map.auto_tick is false so the _accum loop adds 0 and never ticks; only the self-heal refresh can act. It cannot mask the hold or auto_tick behaviour, and does not change sim inputs/journals, so replay/time gates are unaffected; scene-session-audits (incl. playthrough-time and codex-unlocks) and playthrough-ai-modes remained green. Residual risk: it can only heal; a bug where refresh is needed and the engine would not call _process (map hidden/not in tree) is now hidden in the harness.
